passages.provision_quote: Athletic teams or sports designated for "females", "women" or "girls" may not be open to students of the male sex. C. This section does not restrict the eligibility of any student to participate in any interscholastic or intramural athletic team or sport designated as being for "males", "men" or "boys" or designated as "coed" or "mixed".
passages.note: Chapter 106 prints the enacted Senate Engrossed text, which is the version the House passed; it adds one statute section on team designation and names no voter.

rows.reasoning: Carter voted Y on final passage of SB 1165 (2022), a single-subject bill adding one statute section that designates every school athletic team by biological sex and provides that teams "designated for "females", "women" or "girls" may not be open to students of the male sex"; the tally was 31-24, so the vote is not near-unanimous. That operative section is a requirement that transgender athletes play on teams matching their sex at birth, the rung reading "require transgender athletes to compete only on teams matching their biological sex assigned at birth." The bill's own section C leaves boys' and coed teams open to any student, which excludes the rung that would "completely ban all transgender athletes from competing in any organized sports competitions."
